basis: The paragraph opens with the lemma 'Et dominamini piscibus maris, et volatilibus coeli, et universis animantibus quae'. The printing marks neither chapter nor verse, so the extent is the lemma this paragraph opens with, placed by fitting the whole commentary as one non-decreasing walk through Genesis rather than by reading this paragraph alone.
date_basis: Bede's dedicatory letter to Acca of Hexham says the work was undertaken at Acca's asking and first carried only as far as Adam's expulsion from paradise, in two books, and was afterwards extended. Acca held Hexham from 709 to 731. The four-book redaction Migne prints is conventionally placed in the early 720s and the two-book one shortly before it; the range covers both, and no source held here narrows it. The date is the writing, not Migne's 1850 printing.
text: Et dominamini piscibus maris, et volatilibus coeli, et universis animantibus quae moventur super terram. Merito quaeritur in quam utilitatem homo dominatum in pisces, et volucres, et animantia terrae cuncta, perceperit, vel quos ad usus, quaeve solatia, sint haec creata homini, si nunquam peccaret: cui sicut sequentia Scripturae hujus declarant, non haec ad escam sed herbae solum et arborum sunt fructus in prima conditione concessi, nisi forte dicendum est, quia peccaturum presciebat Deus hominem, et mortalem peccando futurum quem immortalem ipse creavit, ideoque ea illi solatia primordialiter instituit, quibus suam fragilitatem mortalis posset tueri, vel alimentum videlicet ex his, vel indumentum, vel laborum, vel itineris, habens adjumentum. Nec quaesitu dignum est quare non etiam nunc cunctis homo dominetur animantibus; postquam enim ipse suo Conditori subjectus esse noluit, perdidit dominium eorum quae suo Conditor juri subjecerat. Denique testimonium primae creationis legimus viris sanctis atque humiliter Deo servientibus et aves obsequium praebuisse, et rictus bestiarum cessisse et venenum nocere non potuisse serpentium.
